title: A product over an initial segment collapses to 1 mod p when a fixed-point-free involution pairs each factor with its inverse
statement: Let p be a positive integer, F : Nat -> Int, and sigma : Nat -> Nat. If sigma is injective on {0..n-1}, maps that set into itself, has NO fixed point there, is an involution there, and pairs factors into inverses (F k * F (sigma k) = 1 mod p for every k < n), then prodRange F n = 1 mod p. PRIMALITY IS NOT REQUIRED AND IS NOT PRESENT. This is a fact about fixed-point-free involutions over any positive modulus; primality enters only downstream, when sigma := Nat.inverseIndex p is supplied and one has to know the pairing exists at all. THE FIXED-POINT-FREE PREMISE IS LOAD-BEARING: without it sigma = id satisfies injectivity, mapsInto and the involution law, and the pairing premise degenerates to F k * F k = 1, from which prodRange F n = 1 does not follow. Equality of indices is Eq on Nat; the conclusion is Int.ModEq. A NOTE ON `AxNat`, because the name is actively misleading: the `Ax` is `axeyum`, not `axiom`. `lean_pp` roots the kernel's COMPUTATIONAL (inductive, constructed) naturals at `AxNat` for one reason only -- so an exported term does not shadow Lean's own `Nat`. It collides badly with `AxReal`, where `Ax` DOES mean axiomatized and the trusted surface is 30. The `nat` prelude measures 0: no Axiom, no Opaque, no Quotient.

formal.statement: theorem Int.prod_range_pairing_collapse : ((x0 : Int) -> ((x1 : Int.lt Int.zero x0) -> ((x2 : AxNat) -> ((x3 : ((x3 : AxNat) -> Int)) -> ((x4 : ((x4 : AxNat) -> AxNat)) -> ((x5 : AxNat.injectiveOn x4 x2) -> ((x6 : AxNat.mapsInto x4 x2) -> ((x7 : ((x7 : AxNat) -> ((x8 : AxNat.lt x7 x2) -> Not (Eq.{1} AxNat (x4 x7) x7)))) -> ((x8 : ((x8 : AxNat) -> ((x9 : AxNat.lt x8 x2) -> Eq.{1} AxNat (x4 (x4 x8)) x8))) -> ((x9 : ((x9 : AxNat) -> ((x10 : AxNat.lt x9 x2) -> Int.ModEq x0 (Int.mul (x3 x9) (x3 (x4 x9))) Int.one))) -> Int.ModEq x0 (Int.prodRange x3 x2) Int.one))))))))))

evidence.supports: `Int.prod_range_pairing_collapse` is admitted with exactly the type in formal.statement. THE INDUCTION IS ORDINARY, AND THAT CORRECTS A PLAN THAT HAD SURVIVED NINE DRAFTS: wilson.rs's module doc sketched strong induction via WellFounded.fix, citing gcd.rs's precedent. It is not needed. The step decreases the domain by exactly 2, so proving `And (family n) (family (succ n))` together by plain Nat.rec suffices. The step conjugates sigma by a two-point transposition. Nat.transposition's helpers are typed concretely over NatDev, so a local IntDev-native copy was built rather than editing a file another lane held; the already-generic conjugate_injective / conjugate_maps_into were reused unchanged.

provenance.established_by: lane agent-capability-assurance (2026-08-24). Seven lanes narrowed to this statement: Int.prodRange_permute removes ONE index per step at the SAME domain size, so unwound it reconstructs the product from itself -- which is why ((p-1)!)^2 = 1 mod p came free and the SIGN did not. This lemma removes a matched PAIR and carries the information. Statement pin and its mutation control added by the coordinating lane.

prior_art.what: the pairing argument underlying Wilson's theorem
prior_art.where: conventionally attributed to Lagrange's first proof of Wilson's theorem
prior_art.attribution: standard attribution; this lane did not consult the primary source. The lemma isolated here is the combinatorial core, stated for an arbitrary fixed-point-free involution rather than for the inverse map of a prime residue system.

notes:
WHAT IS NOT PROVED, stated so it is not inferred: WILSON'S THEOREM. This is the induction Wilson needs, not Wilson. What remains is wiring: sigma := Nat.inverseIndex p has TWO fixed points on {0..p-2}, namely 0 and p-2 (Nat.inverseIndex_fixed_point already establishes there are no others), so the collapse applies to the INTERIOR only, after those two are excised with Nat.restrict_pair. The missing named equations are sigma 0 = 0 and sigma (p-2) = p-2.

A METHODOLOGICAL CORRECTION WORTH KEEPING: Nat.setwise_fixed and Nat.restrict_pair were built for this lemma and turned out to be the wrong tool for it -- they remove sigma's own FIXED points, while this induction removes a matched SWAP pair, a different operation. They are not wasted; they are what the interior excision above will need. But a slice was dispatched on a mistaken account of what the induction required.

One real bug, found by bisection and recorded because the class has cost eight lanes in a day: InjectiveOn's Pi groups VALUES before PROOFS (forall a b, a<n -> b<n -> ...), and an early draft interleaved them. Visible only through the fully assembled term; cargo check --lib never runs Kernel::add_declaration and cannot see it.

The proof is constructive throughout: no Classical.em, no propext, no funext, no Quot.sound. Notably it does NOT use WellFounded.fix either.

external_status is `proved`: the pairing argument is classical. What is locally new is only that it is isolated as a standalone lemma about involutions rather than entangled with the residue-system specifics.
